title: WRAP for Your Workplace:
title_short: WRAP for Your Workplace · What does ‘not okay’ look like?
headline: WRAP makes a team better at noticing each other. A 60-second promo asking other organizations to bring WRAP to their staff.
story: Madison is good at hiding when she's struggling. Her coworkers know when she's quiet and closed off, that's not her.
WRAP lets a group name what everyone looks like when they're well and not well. A coworker without her usual morning drink gets a “hey, are you doing OK?”
WRAP made Madison a better coworker. Her pitch to other organizations: bring it to your employees. Peer support doesn't come with conditions.
do: Open on the whiteboard feelings list with the hook text.
Show the WRAP group when she talks about the group; show a coworker when she names one.
Cut her filler (“So”, “I think”, “you know”); captions match what's left.
End card: “Bring WRAP to your team.” + mha-ne.org + logo, 4 s.
dont: Not a sign-up video for individuals. No “register here”.
No therapy, treatment or clinical words.
No participant face without a signed release. No minors.
No desk, keyboard or paper filler B-roll.

bp_intro: Voice is all 20260909_C4587.MP4 (Madison, 22:22, pink MHA shirt). B-roll from the WRAP group (C4588–C4613) and office (C4504–C4522). Times are from the Day 1 per-clip transcript. Interviews 24 fps, B-roll 50 fps.

rows.visual: C4601 00:00: the whiteboard with the feelings list, facilitator with curly hair in front of it.
rows.motion: Hook text on frame 1, big and bold: What does ‘not okay’ look like? No logo, no name plate.

voice.quote: So I'm really good at hiding when I'm struggling.

rows.visual: Madison on camera (pink MHA shirt, glasses, MHA sign). At about 0:10 cut to C4506 00:00: two women in chairs in a dim office, talking.
rows.motion: Super once, lower corner, 3 s: “Madison Herman · Peer Support Specialist & WRAP Facilitator, MHA Nebraska”.

voice.quote: If I come to work and I'm really quiet and closed off, and I have headphones in, and I'm not trying to small talk, and my coworkers know that that's not me.

rows.visual: C4593 00:00: facilitator in white shirt and green scarf, gesturing. Then C4590 00:00: bearded man and woman with glasses at the table.

voice.quote: It's a really good way to come together as a group and identify what everybody looks like when they're doing well and what everybody looks like when they're not well.

rows.visual: C4588 00:00: young woman at a table with her worksheet. Then C4589 00:00: two women at a table, tablet and notebook.

voice.quote: One of my coworkers is a very big routine person and gets the same drink every single morning from the gas station. … If I see her in the morning and she doesn't have that drink, I'm going to make a comment like, hey, are you doing OK?

rows.visual: C4598 00:00: the whiteboard safety agreement. Then C4607 00:00: the facilitator writing on the whiteboard.

voice.quote: If I didn't take a WRAP group with her, I wouldn't have known that because we're so used to being in our own world where we have our own routines and we don't pick up on things like that.
I know for 100% fact it has made me a better coworker. I am more approachable. I'm more reliable because I feel better about myself and my routine and my performance.

rows.visual: C4612 00:00: facilitator at the flip chart. Then C4604 00:00: man in green shirt speaking at the table.
rows.motion: Small text card: <q>WRAP · Wellness Recovery Action Plan</q>.

voice.quote: If you are thinking about bringing WRAP to your organization, I highly recommend it, not only for the participants, but for your employees.
Peer support is powerful because it doesn't come with conditions.

rows.motion: <q>Bring WRAP to your team.</q> + mha-ne.org + MHA Nebraska logo. Hold 4 s.
